## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D round-based zombie shooter with a Fortnite-style feel.

## Requirements
- Build the game now without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- Check screenshots using JPEGs no wider than 1280px; read only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires PNG.

## Decisions
- Created an original third-person survival game, “Deadzone — Last Stand,” with wave-based zombie combat, building, and battle-royale-inspired HUD styling.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented 3D arena, player movement and aiming, weapons/ammo/reload, zombies and waves, health/shield, building, pickups, pause/game-over flows, responsive HUD, and touch controls.
- `npm run build` succeeds.
- Visually checked the initial menu and in-game scene via `screenshots/current.jpg`; gameplay controls were exercised.
- Added an inline SVG favicon to `index.html`.

### Active
- Verify the favicon change and optionally re-run the build/browser check; the last edit occurred after the screenshot check.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `npm run build`.
2. Reload the browser and verify there are no application errors or favicon 404s; update `screenshots/current.jpg` if checking visuals.
3. Finish with a brief description of the game and its assumed controls/style.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, menus, HUD, and inline favicon.
- `src/main.js`: Three.js scene, gameplay systems, controls, and game state.
- `src/style.css`: Visual design and responsive layout.
- `package.json`: Vite scripts and Three.js dependency.
- `screenshots/current.jpg`: Latest saved visual check.

## Important Context
- Latest browser console showed only a favicon 404 and Three.js warnings; an inline data-URI favicon was added afterward.
- Browser console also reported `THREE.Clock` deprecated and that `PCFSoftShadowMap` was removed; neither stopped gameplay.
- Changes are uncommitted.
